items.title: Private Inference enters a limited customer test
items.summary: Sam Altman says OpenAI is testing Private Inference with a small group of customers. The company describes confidential computing and access controls; this is a limited test, not general availability or independent proof of its security.
items.sourceName: OpenAI · product page; post checked through public archive

items.title: Candidate planets still need confirmation
items.summary: OpenAI describes two amateur astronomy searches using Codex and Astra with public telescope data. The signals are candidates for professional follow-up, not confirmed discoveries.
items.sourceName: OpenAI · company account; post checked through public archive

items.title: A temporary shield while a Linux patch is prepared
items.summary: OpenAI announces Shirudo with Cisco. Operators test and approve temporary protections for running Linux services; the company’s demonstration is not evidence that every workload is protected.
items.sourceName: OpenAI · announcement; post checked through public archive

items.title: OpenWorks offers local help through a U.S. pilot
items.summary: OpenAI invites independent small businesses and local AI practitioners to apply. The pilot has eligibility and location limits; a partner stipend is a maximum offer, not guaranteed income.
items.sourceName: OpenAI · program requirements; post checked through public archive

items.title: Altman backs a discussion of common limits
items.summary: Sam Altman endorses Pachocki’s proposal and hopes laboratories can agree on common limits. This is support for an approach, not evidence that a new limit has been agreed or implemented.

items.title: OpenAI explains its anti-distillation safeguards
items.summary: OpenAI describes defenses against extracting protected reasoning and copying capabilities into other models. Its reported improvements come from internal evaluations; they do not establish that extraction or misuse is impossible.

items.title: GPT-Live-1.1 reaches the API
items.summary: OpenAI Developers announces the voice model’s API release and a lower-cost standby option for WebRTC calls. Standby still incurs charges, and backend model and tool usage is billed separately.

items.title: File access and network access are separate choices
items.summary: OpenAI Developers explains the Codex sandbox’s filesystem and network boundaries. The engineering article also describes its limitations; sandboxing is one protection, not a guarantee against every harmful action.

items.title: Brockman shares ChatGPT for Accounting
items.summary: Greg Brockman highlights the new accounting workflow. OpenAI’s examples prepare invoices and reconciliation material for review; people still need to check records, calculations and coding before approval.
items.sourceName: OpenAI · product page and stated controls

items.title: Altman welcomes GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
items.summary: Sam Altman emphasizes token efficiency and Sol’s ultrafast option. This is the CEO’s assessment of the launch; the linked system card also describes remaining limitations.

items.title: An updated view of API usage and errors
items.summary: OpenAI Developers says the Analytics dashboard now surfaces spending, rate-limited requests and errors by model, project or API key. Useful for investigating usage; a dashboard view is not a spending cap.

items.title: Outside assessors get deeper access
items.summary: OpenAI announces assessments with Apollo Research, METR, Transluce and Goodfire. Its protocols allow publication with confidentiality redactions and possible disclosure delays; these are planned assessments, not completed safety findings.
